name: Slow Cooker Beef and Potato Au Gratin Casserole
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified on the card at 556 cal / 35g protein per serving at 6 servings, so it clears the bar as written with no adjustment. Seven cheap board ingredients total and it layers rather than assembles, which is ideal for batch. Confidence: high, nutrition read off the recipe card. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Five ingredients. That is the entire list. Ground beef, sliced potatoes, onion, cheddar, and a splash of broth, layered into a slow cooker and left alone until the potatoes go tender and the cheese melts down through all of it. This is the cheapest dinner in this batch and one of the cheapest on the whole site. Each serving carries 34 grams of protein and 569 calories for about $1.99.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (paprika, garlic powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.20. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $27.80 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.99 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $33.63 across 14 servings, roughly $2.40 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $8.47 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $42.10. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $1.99 a serving. Under two dollars for a hot dinner with real meat and real cheese in it, which is the kind of number that makes the case for cooking all on its own.
shop_smart: Potatoes are the volume and the value. Buy the biggest bag you will get through, since the per pound price drops steeply with size and they keep for weeks in a cool dark spot.
Shredded cheddar goes on sale constantly. Buy the bags when they drop and freeze what you will not use this week, because it melts perfectly fine after thawing.
Slicing the potatoes thin and even matters more here than in any other recipe in this batch. Uneven slices mean some are mush while others are still hard.
Ground beef is the only line that moves the number much. Everything else on this list is a dollar or two.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet with the paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until no pink remains, then drain the fat.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thin and even, about an eighth of an inch. A mandoline is fastest, a steady hand and a sharp knife works.
Slice the onion thin as well.
Layer half the potatoes in the slow cooker, then half the onion, half the beef, and a third of the cheddar. Repeat the layers.
Pour the chicken broth over the top and finish with the last of the cheddar.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until a knife goes through the potatoes with no resistance.
Turn the cooker off and let it sit uncovered 15 minutes so the layers set enough to lift out cleanly.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Cut the set casserole into portions of roughly that weight and lift them into 14 containers so the layers stay intact. Each serving lands at 569 calories with 34 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from themagicalslowcooker.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A hot dinner for about $1.99 a serving. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Slow cooker beef and potato au gratin meal prep: layered ground beef, thin sliced potatoes, onion, and cheddar cooked 6 hours. 569 calories, 34g protein, about $1.99 per serving.
head.keywords: beef and potato au gratin, slow cooker casserole, cheesy potato beef bake, ground beef casserole, budget meal prep, cheap dinners
steps: Brown the ground beef with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper, then drain.
Slice the potatoes and onion thin and even.
Layer potatoes, onion, beef, and cheddar into the slow cooker twice.
Pour over the chicken broth, top with the last cheddar, and cook on low 6 hours.
Rest 15 minutes uncovered, then cut and portion into 14 containers.
